title: Choose the word which best expresses the meaning of given
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word which best expresses the meaning of given word

Dreadfully
solution:
Answer: Incredibly

Explanation: 'Dreadfully' is commonly used as an intensifier meaning 'extremely' or 'very'. 'Incredibly' conveys the same intensifying idea, so it is the best match.

  • Why 'Incredibly' is correct: It expresses a high degree or intensity (e.g., "She was dreadfully tired" = "She was incredibly tired").

  • Why 'Disastrous' is incorrect: It means causing a disaster or great damage and is an adjective, not an adverb that intensifies.

  • Why 'Sad' is incorrect: It denotes feeling sorrow or unhappiness and does not match the intensifying sense of 'dreadfully'.

  • Why 'none of above' is incorrect: A correct synonym is present among the choices, so selecting 'none of above' is not appropriate.

optionFeedback.html: Correct. 'Dreadfully' is often used as an intensifier meaning 'extremely' or 'very', so 'Incredibly' best matches this sense.
'Disastrous' is incorrect. It means causing great damage or disaster (an adjective describing events), not an adverb meaning 'very' or 'extremely'.
'Sad' is incorrect. It means feeling sorrow or unhappiness and does not convey the intensifying sense of 'dreadfully'.
'None of above' is incorrect because one of the given choices ('Incredibly') correctly matches the intensifying meaning of 'dreadfully'.

title: Choose the word that does not belong to the group.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the word that does not belong to the group.
solution:
Correct answer: Imbue — it is a verb, not a type of building or structure.

  • Barrack: a building used to house soldiers (a military housing structure).

  • Duplex: a residential building divided into two separate living units.

  • Gazebo: a freestanding outdoor pavilion or small structure, typically found in a garden.

  • Imbue: a verb meaning to fill or permeate with a quality or feeling (to inspire); it refers to an action/quality rather than a physical structure.

Because the first three words are types of structures and the fourth is a verb, the fourth word does not belong in the group.

optionFeedback.html: Barrack is a building used to house soldiers (a military housing structure). It is a type of structure, so it belongs with duplex and gazebo.
Duplex is a residential building divided into two separate living units. It is a type of structure, so it belongs with barrack and gazebo.
Gazebo is a freestanding outdoor pavilion or small structure often found in gardens. It is a type of structure, so it belongs with barrack and duplex.
Imbue is a verb meaning to fill, permeate, or inspire (to impart a quality). It is not a physical structure, so it is the odd one out.

title: Both the countries have tried their best to have relationship
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Both the countries have tried their best to have a ______ relationship between them but the constraints of domestic politics have often ______ their bilateral mutual relationship.
solution: The answer is option (D). Both the countries have tried to have a friendly (cordial) relationship; the use of 'but' suggests that these efforts have not been successful, since political constraints have concealed/shadowed (eclipsed) their relationship.

title: His explanations made the complex topic easy to understand.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: His __________ explanations made the complex topic easy to understand.
solution:
Answer: Succinct — brief and clearly expressed. Succinct explanations are concise yet clear, which makes a complex topic easier to understand.

Why the other choices are wrong:

  • convoluted — means extremely complex and hard to follow; such explanations would hinder understanding.

  • complicated — suggests many interrelated difficulties; it does not imply clarity or simplicity.

  • perplexing — means confusing or puzzling; such explanations would leave readers baffled.

Tip: For sentences that say something made a topic easy to understand, choose a word that implies clarity and brevity (for example, succinct or concise).

optionFeedback.html: Incorrect. "Convoluted" means extremely complex and hard to follow. If explanations were convoluted, they would make the topic harder to understand, not easier.
Correct. "Succinct" means brief and clearly expressed. Succinct explanations are concise yet clear, which helps make a complex topic easy to understand.
Incorrect. "Complicated" means involving many interrelated parts or difficulties. Describing explanations as complicated suggests they would be harder to follow, not helpful for understanding.
Incorrect. "Perplexing" means causing confusion or puzzlement. Perplexing explanations would leave readers confused rather than helping them understand.

title: Disagreement always indicates

solution:

title: Teetotaller is one
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: A Teetotaller is one

Definition and Concept

A Teetotaller specifically refers to someone who completely avoids alcohol consumption, not just reducing intake. Review the prefix 'teeto-' which historically relates to total abstinence from intoxicating beverages.

This option describes someone who leaves their religion. A Teetotaller specifically refers to abstinence from alcohol, not religious abandonment. Check the root word 'teetotal' which relates to drinking habits.

title: Choose the word that best replaces the words highlighted in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that best replaces the quoted phrase in the sentence.

The children in the playschool were playing with “one half of a sphere”.
solution:
CONCEPT

A one-word substitution replaces a descriptive phrase with a noun that preserves the phrase’s exact meaning and grammatical role.

Word parts can help: the prefix hemi- means “half”, and sphere names a completely round three-dimensional solid.

APPLICATION

The quoted phrase describes one of the two equal halves of a sphere. Combining hemi- with sphere gives hemisphere, the noun for either such half.

CONTRAST

  • A globe is a spherical object or model, especially a representation of Earth.

  • A cylinder has two parallel circular bases joined by a curved surface.

  • A sphere is the complete round solid rather than one of its halves.

RESULT

The best replacement is “a hemisphere”.

optionFeedback.html: The noun “globe” denotes a spherical object or model, especially a representation of Earth.
The noun “cylinder” denotes a solid with two parallel circular bases joined by a curved surface.
The noun “sphere” denotes a completely round three-dimensional solid whose surface points are equidistant from its centre.
The noun “hemisphere” denotes either half of a sphere divided by a plane through its centre.

title: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her _______ manner of speaking made it difficult for people to understand her true feelings.
solution:
The blank needs a word describing a manner of speaking that made it hard for people to grasp her true feelings — i.e. a manner that is unclear or open to several interpretations.

“Ambiguous” means open to more than one interpretation, vague or unclear; an ambiguous manner of speaking naturally leaves listeners uncertain of the real meaning, matching the clue “difficult to understand her true feelings.”

The other words point the wrong way: “forthright” (direct, frank), “candid” (honest, open) and “effusive” (gushing, openly emotional) all describe speech that reveals feelings clearly, so they contradict the context. Hence “ambiguous” is the most appropriate choice.

optionFeedback.html: “Forthright” describes someone who is direct, frank and outspoken. A forthright manner reveals a person’s views and feelings plainly, so it would make her feelings easier to read, not harder — the opposite of what the sentence requires.

“Effusive” means expressing emotion in an unrestrained, gushing way. An effusive speaker pours out feelings openly, which would make her emotions obvious rather than concealed, so it does not match the sense of the sentence.
“Candid” means honest, open and straightforward. A candid manner of speaking exposes one’s genuine feelings clearly, so it conflicts with the idea that her true feelings were hard to understand.

“Ambiguous” means open to more than one interpretation, unclear or vague. An ambiguous manner of speaking leaves listeners unsure of what is really meant, which fits a sentence about feelings that are difficult to understand.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q9
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Direction: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the underlined word.

The government introduced several measures to alleviate poverty in rural areas.
solution:
Concept: A synonym question asks for the word that carries the same core sense as the underlined word, so that substituting it preserves the sentence’s meaning. “Alleviate” means to make a problem, hardship, or burden less severe or intense — to lessen its degree, not to remove it fully.

Application: In “The government introduced several measures to alleviate poverty in rural areas,” alleviate describes the intended effect of the measures on poverty: making its severity smaller. Substituting “reduce” — “measures to reduce poverty” — keeps this exact sense of lessening a problem’s extent, so the sentence’s meaning is preserved.

Cross-check: Checking each remaining word against this same sense of lessening severity rules them out:

  • “Increase” denotes a rise in quantity, size, or degree — the reverse of lessening something — so substituting it would flip the sentence’s meaning.

  • “Observe” denotes watching, noticing, or remarking on something, with no sense of a change in magnitude at all.

  • “Ignore” denotes deliberately disregarding something; disregarding a problem does not make it less severe.

So “reduce” is the word that keeps “alleviate”’s sense of lessening severity intact in this sentence.

optionFeedback.html: Increase typically describes sales, population, temperature, or output becoming greater than before.
Reduce typically describes costs, risk, delay, or waste becoming smaller than before.
Observe typically describes a rule being followed, a ritual being performed, or a process or someone’s behaviour being watched closely.
Ignore typically describes a warning, request, rule, or fact being disregarded.

title: TPSC Senior Computer Assistant — 2026 — Q6
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to “UBIQUITOUS”.
solution:
Concept

Synonyms are words that have the same or nearly the same meaning in a given context.

To choose the nearest synonym, identify the core sense of the target word and compare it with each offered word, noting contrasts such as frequency, quantity, uniqueness, and extent of presence.

Application

Ubiquitous describes something that seems to be present or found everywhere. Omnipresent carries the same central idea of being present everywhere, so it is the nearest match.

Contrast and cross-check

  • Rare means seldom encountered; it concerns low frequency.

  • Scarce means insufficiently available; it concerns limited quantity.

  • Unique means being the only one of its kind; it concerns singularity.

Therefore, the nearest synonym is Omnipresent.

optionFeedback.html: Rare describes something encountered only infrequently.
Scarce describes something available in an insufficient or limited quantity.
This adjective is used for something without a comparable counterpart in its category.
Omnipresent describes something that is present everywhere at the same time.

title: Which of the following best describes the word ossification?
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Which of the following best describes the word ossification?
solution:
Correct answer: Hardening

Explanation:

  • Definition: Ossification is the process of bone formation — the replacement or transformation of tissue into bone or bone-like (hardened) material.

  • Context: It occurs normally during skeletal development (intramembranous and endochondral ossification). In clinical contexts, ossification can also refer to abnormal calcification or hardening of soft tissues.

optionFeedback.html: Correct. Ossification refers to the process of forming bone or bone-like tissue — in common terms, it means hardening (the conversion of tissue into bone or calcified material).
Incorrect. Plasticity means the ability of a material to be shaped or deformed without breaking; it does not refer to the formation of bone or hardening into bone.
Incorrect. Ambition refers to a desire to achieve something or succeed; it is unrelated to biological processes like bone formation.
Incorrect. Incorporation means including or combining something into a whole; it does not describe the process of bone formation or hardening into bone.

title: What is synonymy relation?
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Which statement defines the semantic relation of synonymy?
solution:
Concept

Lexical-semantic relations describe how the meanings of words or expressions are connected.

Synonymy is the relation in which two expressions have the same or nearly the same meaning; substitutability can still depend on context and register.

Application

The statement “A denotes the same as B” directly expresses equality or near-equality of meaning, so it represents synonymy.

Contrast

  • “A is part of B” expresses a part–whole relation, known as meronymy.

  • “A is a kind of B” places A under the broader class B, which is hyponymy.

  • “A is superordinate of B” makes A the broader class that includes B, which is hypernymy.

Cross-check

Pairs such as “begin” and “start” can denote the same action in many contexts, confirming the synonymy criterion.

Result: A denotes the same as B.

optionFeedback.html: In “a wheel is part of a car,” wheel names a component and car names the whole that contains it.
The paired verbs occur in parallel sentences: “Classes begin at nine” and “Classes start at nine.” The example keeps the event and time constant.
In “a rose is a flower,” rose names a narrower class and flower names the broader class containing it.
In “vehicles include cars,” vehicle names the broader class and car names the narrower class included within it.

title: In the given two sentences, select from the answer choice
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:

(i) The organisation was established at the beginning of this century.

(ii) The little girl could not twist the cap off the bottles.
solution:
Contextual Analysis
Sentence (i): "The organisation was established at the beginning of this century."

The term "beginning" refers to the start or origin. None of the options (Crack, Break, Loosen, Turn) serve as a synonym for "beginning" in this sentence.

Sentence (ii): "The little girl could not twist the cap off the bottles."

The term "twist" refers to a rotational movement. Among the choices, "Turn" (Option D) is a synonym for "twist" in this context.

optionFeedback.html: Incorrect. "Crack" does not synonymize with "beginning" or "twist" in these specific sentences.
Incorrect. "Break" does not align with the temporal meaning of the first sentence or the rotational meaning of the second.
Incorrect. While "loosen" might be used for the second sentence, it is not a standard replacement for the "beginning" of a century.
Correct. "Turn" serves as a standard idiomatic expression for the start of a century and a mechanical synonym for twisting a cap.

optionFeedback.html: This is the correct choice because it fits both contexts accurately.
This fits the first sentence ("the stadium can hold...") but does not make sense in the second ("Mohan is willing to hold his tour programme").
While this could fit the second sentence, it is not a suitable substitute for "seat" in the first sentence.
This does not work as a synonym for either "seat" or "adjust" in these contexts.

title: Choose which of the following is closest to the word

title: Find the synonyms of the following word Explicit

Antonym questions test whether you know a word's core sense precisely enough to state its exact opposite — not just any word that looks or sounds related. The highlighted word “proceed” means to move forward or carry on in a course of action. Reversing this specific sense of forward movement gives “to move backward, withdraw, or go away” — exactly what “receding” expresses.

  • proceeding — carries the same forward-moving sense as the highlighted word, so it is a near-synonym, not an opposite.

  • succeeding — means coming after in sequence or achieving a goal; this concerns order, not direction of movement.

  • preceding — means coming before in sequence; again an order relationship, not the movement-direction opposite required here.

Because “receding” is the only option that reverses the specific sense of forward movement carried by “proceed,” it is the correct antonym.

optionFeedback.html: “Proceeding” carries the same forward-moving sense as the highlighted word, making it a near-synonym rather than its opposite.

  • “Short” — opposite of long; about length, not bending.

Only crooked reverses the property of being direct/unbent, which is why it is the correct antonym.

optionFeedback.html: “Weak” is the opposite of “strong,” describing a lack of physical or moral strength. It belongs to the dimension of strength or power, an entirely different category from the word given here.

“Short” is the opposite of “long”; it belongs to the dimension of length or extent, describing how much there is. That is a different category from the word given here.

title: Select the ANTONYM of the given word. DESPAIR
subject: Verbal Ability (English)

solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is the direct opposite of a given word along the same idea. To find one, first fix the core meaning of the target word, then choose the option that expresses the reverse of that same idea — not merely a word that is negative or unrelated.

Application

DESPAIR means the complete loss of hope — a feeling that nothing good will happen. Its meaning lives on the axis of hope vs. hopelessness. The opposite end of that same axis is the expectation that something good will happen, i.e. hope.

Contrast

  • Hope — belief that a good outcome will come; this sits at the opposite end of the hope/hopelessness axis from despair, so it is the antonym.

  • Detest — to strongly dislike someone or something; this is about aversion, a different axis altogether from hope.

  • Abandon — to leave behind or give up on something; an action concerning desertion, not the emotional state of hopelessness.

  • Reject — to refuse or turn down something offered; about refusal, again unrelated to the loss-of-hope idea.

optionFeedback.html: “Detest” means to strongly dislike or feel aversion toward someone or something. Aversion is a different idea from despair (a state of dejection), so detest is not its opposite.
“Abandon” means to leave behind or give up on something — an action of desertion. Despair names an emotional state, not an action, so abandon does not reverse its meaning.
“Reject” means to refuse or turn down something that is offered. Refusal is a different idea from despair (a state of dejection), so reject is not its antonym.
“Hope” is the belief that a good outcome will happen. It sits at the opposite end of the same hope/hopelessness axis as despair, making it the direct antonym.

The word 'abundant' implies a large quantity rather than just meeting needs. Check if the synonym captures excess or richness in amount instead of mere adequacy.

title: Select the word which is closest to the opposite in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the word which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word.

He has penchant for writing satirical poems.
solution:
To determine the correct antonym, we must first clearly define the word "penchant" in the context of the sentence.

Word Analysis
Penchant: A strong or habitual liking for something or a tendency to do something.

Sentence context: "He has a penchant (strong liking/preference) for writing satirical poems."

Antonym required: We need a word that represents a lack of preference, aversion, or dislike for something.

optionFeedback.html: Penchant means a strong liking or preference for something. Since the question asks for an opposite, dislike correctly represents aversion rather than attraction.

The word bias refers to a prejudice or inclination, not necessarily an opposite of liking. Penchant indicates a strong preference, so you should look for a term expressing aversion or lack of interest instead.
Repulsion is a strong feeling of disgust or aversion. While it relates to dislike, the question asks for the closest opposite of penchant, which means a strong liking or preference.
Hatred is an intense dislike or hostility. Although it opposes liking, penchant specifically refers to a strong preference rather than general affection.

title: Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted word in the sentence.

The programme was not organized properly and confusion seemed inevitable.
solution:
Key idea: “Inevitable” means certain to happen or unavoidable.

  • The opposite idea is something that is not certain.

  • “Uncertain” best expresses that opposite meaning.

Answer: Option 0, “uncertain”, is correct.

optionFeedback.html: Correct. “Uncertain” is the opposite of inevitable.
Incorrect. “Sufficient” means enough.
Incorrect. “Permanent” means lasting.
Incorrect. “Appropriate” means suitable.

title: Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that means the opposite of the word in bold in the sentence.

The leading English newspapers are known for their comprehensive coverage of news.
solution:
CONCEPT

An antonym is a word whose meaning contrasts with the central sense of another word in its context.

For an adjective describing coverage, compare the choices on the same semantic axis: breadth, completeness, or sufficiency.

APPLICATION

Here, “comprehensive” describes coverage that includes all or nearly all relevant news. Its contextual opposite is coverage that is insufficient in scope; “inadequate” carries that meaning.

CONTRAST

  • “Indifferent” describes a lack of interest or concern, so it belongs to the axis of attitude.

  • “Difficult” describes something hard to do or understand, so it belongs to the axis of effort.

  • “Impossible” describes something that cannot happen or be done, so it belongs to the axis of possibility.

  • “Inadequate” describes something insufficient in quality, quantity, or scope, so it belongs to the axis of sufficiency.

RESULT

The opposite of “comprehensive” in this sentence is “inadequate.”

optionFeedback.html: “Indifferent” describes a lack of interest or concern; its semantic axis is attitude.
“Difficult” describes something hard to do or understand; its semantic axis is effort or complexity.
“Impossible” describes something that cannot happen or be done; its semantic axis is possibility or feasibility.
“Inadequate” describes something insufficient for a need; its semantic axis is sufficiency or adequacy.

title: Choose the word that roughly means the same as the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that roughly means the same as the underlined phrase in the sentence.

The committee's decision to fund the project was agreed upon by everyone in the committee.
solution:
CONCEPT

A synonym is a word whose meaning is the same as, or very close to, another word or phrase in a particular context.

Context clues identify the intended sense; a word that is merely related to the topic is not necessarily interchangeable.

APPLICATION

The highlighted phrase describes complete agreement among all members of a group. “Unanimous” expresses that shared agreement, so it preserves the sentence’s meaning.

CONTRAST

  • “Divisive” describes something that creates disagreement or separation.

  • “Decided” describes something settled or determined, without saying that every person agreed.

  • “Comprehensive” describes something broad or complete in scope.

CROSS-CHECK

Substitution gives: “The committee’s decision to fund the project was unanimous.” The sentence still states that all committee members agreed, confirming “unanimous” as the result.

optionFeedback.html: “Unanimous” is an adjective commonly modifying collective outcomes such as votes, verdicts, and decisions.
“Divisive” is an adjective commonly modifying issues, proposals, or rhetoric that split opinion.
“Decided” is an adjective commonly modifying a settled view, result, or advantage.
“Comprehensive” is an adjective commonly modifying reports or plans that cover a wide scope.

title: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The deserted streets brought about a morose feeling into our minds.
solution:
The word 'morose' means gloomy, sullen, ill-humoured, or depressed in mood. We need its antonym (opposite).

'happy' (cheerful, light-hearted) directly opposes the gloomy sense of 'morose', so it is the correct antonym.

'sympathetic' (compassionate toward others) and 'diseased' (ill) describe attitude and health, not mood; 'halting' (hesitant, faltering) describes speech or movement. None of these is the opposite of 'morose'.

optionFeedback.html: 'Morose' means gloomy, sullen, or depressed in mood. Consider whether this word's meaning is the direct opposite of that gloomy mood.
'Sympathetic' means showing compassion or understanding toward others. It describes an attitude to people, not a mood, so it is not the opposite of 'morose'.
'Diseased' means affected by illness. It is unrelated to a person's gloomy or cheerful state of mind, so it cannot be the antonym of 'morose'.
'Halting' means hesitant or faltering, often describing speech or movement. It does not describe a mood and so is not the opposite of 'morose'.

title: Choose the word which is closest in meaning to the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word which is closest in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence.

Bengaluru has a salubrious climate to live in.
solution:
The sentence describes Bengaluru’s climate as “salubrious.” The word salubrious (from Latin salubris, “healthful, wholesome”) means favourable to health or well-being, and it is used especially of climate or air.

Therefore the closest synonym is “healthful” — a healthful climate is one that is good for your health, exactly the idea conveyed by salubrious.

The other options do not fit: “luxurious” relates to comfort and wealth, “hectic” means very busy or frantic, and “unpredictable” means changeable or hard to forecast — none of these carry the sense of being good for one’s health.

optionFeedback.html: “Healthful” means favourable to good health or well-being. A salubrious place or climate is one that is healthy and good for you — from Latin salubris, “healthful, wholesome.” Compare this sense of physical wholesomeness against the other choices.

“Luxurious” describes great comfort, richness, or expensive elegance — it speaks to wealth and indulgence, not to health. “Salubrious” is specifically about being good for one’s health, so a focus on luxury misses its core meaning.
“Hectic” means very busy, frantic, or full of frenzied activity. That conveys a fast, stressful pace, which is unrelated to the health-promoting quality that “salubrious” describes.

“Unpredictable” means changeable or hard to forecast. While weather can be unpredictable, “salubrious” does not refer to variability — it refers to being beneficial to health, so this is off the mark.

title: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

What a deceitful man; I am happy that he is behind the bars now.
solution:
The underlined word "deceitful" means dishonest, misleading, or intending to cheat. We need its antonym (opposite).

"Honest" means truthful, sincere, and free from deceit, which is the exact opposite of "deceitful." Hence, "honest" is the correct answer.

The other options do not fit: "fortunate" means lucky, "tasteful" means showing good taste, and "diseased" means affected by illness — none of these relate to truthfulness.

optionFeedback.html: "Fortunate" means lucky or favoured by good fortune. It describes circumstances of luck, a sense unrelated to the idea of being truthful or untruthful.
"Tasteful" means showing good aesthetic judgement or refinement in style. It concerns taste and propriety, not a person's honesty.
"Diseased" means affected by illness or unhealthy. It describes a state of physical health, not a trait of character such as truthfulness.
"Honest" means truthful, sincere, and free from deceit. It describes a person who does not mislead or cheat others.

title: Which of the following words used in the passage reinforces
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Which of the following words used in the passage reinforces the idea contained in the word, 'DISSONANCE'?
solution:
Concept

This is a vocabulary-in-context question testing the synonym relationship between words. To 'reinforce the idea' of a key word, an option must share or strengthen its core sense. The word DISSONANCE means a harsh, inharmonious clash of sounds, or a lack of harmony and agreement.

Application

Compare each candidate's core meaning against the sense of discord and harsh, jarring sound carried by DISSONANCE:

  • Cacophony means a harsh, jarring mixture of discordant sounds. This is the same sense of clashing, unharmonious noise that DISSONANCE expresses, so it directly reinforces the idea.

  • Aspersions means false or damaging accusations against someone's character; it concerns slander, not sound or harmony.

  • Strategy means a careful plan of action designed to reach a goal; it has no connection to harmony or noise.

  • Transition means the process of changing from one state to another; it concerns change, not discord.

Cross-check

Only one option carries the 'lack of harmony / harsh sound' sense that defines DISSONANCE. Cacophony is the matching synonym (both are listed together as near-synonyms in standard dictionaries), so it is the word that reinforces the idea contained in DISSONANCE.

optionFeedback.html: Aspersions are false or damaging remarks made to attack someone's reputation, as in 'he cast aspersions on her honesty'. The word belongs to the vocabulary of slander and criticism of character.
Cacophony is a harsh, jarring mixture of discordant sounds, as in 'a cacophony of car horns'. The word belongs to the vocabulary of clashing, unharmonious noise and lack of musical harmony.
Strategy is a carefully devised plan of action for reaching a goal, as in 'a winning strategy for the match'. The word belongs to the vocabulary of planning, tactics and decision-making.

Transition is the process of changing or passing from one state, stage or place to another, as in 'the transition from school to college'. The word belongs to the vocabulary of change and movement over time.

title: Synonym (Most nearest meaning) of ORATOR is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Synonym (most nearly the same meaning) of ORATOR is
solution:
Concept

A synonym is a word that carries nearly the same core meaning as the target word. For vocabulary derived from Latin/Greek roots, fix the root sense first, then match the option whose definition overlaps that sense most closely.

Application

ORATOR comes from the Latin orare (‘to speak, to plead before an assembly’). An orator is therefore a public speaker — someone who delivers a formal, eloquent speech to an audience. Among the options, ‘Speaker’ denotes exactly a person who speaks to an audience, so it shares the central meaning.

Contrast

  • Reader — one who reads written text; about reading, not addressing an audience by speech.

  • Singer — one who produces music with the voice; melody, not spoken oratory.

  • Critic — one who evaluates or judges works; analysis, not public speaking.

Only ‘Speaker’ overlaps the root sense of delivering speech to an audience, so it is the nearest synonym of ORATOR.

optionFeedback.html: 'Speaker' denotes a person who delivers a formal address to an audience, especially in a public or ceremonial setting.
'Reader' denotes a person who reads written material, typically silently for their own comprehension or aloud for others.
'Singer' denotes a person who performs vocal music, producing melody through singing.
'Critic' denotes a person who evaluates and comments on the merit of creative, literary, or intellectual works.

title: Antonym (Most opposite meaning) of the word CELESTIAL is
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Antonym (Most opposite meaning) of the word CELESTIAL is
solution:
Concept

An antonym is the word whose meaning is most opposite to the given word. "Celestial" is an adjective meaning relating to the sky or the heavens — divine, heavenly, otherworldly. So its antonym must name what belongs to the ground/earth, not to the heavens.

Application

CELESTIAL = of the heavens / sky. The opposite domain is the earth / worldly realm. The choice that means "belonging to the earth, worldly, terrestrial" is the correct antonym — that is "Earthly."

Contrast with the near-misses

  • "Heavenly" means of or like heaven — a synonym of celestial, not its opposite.

  • "Divine" means godlike / sacred — again a synonym of the heavenly sense, not an antonym.

  • "Supernatural" means beyond the natural / otherworldly — close in sense to celestial, so it is not the opposite either.

Only "Earthly" reverses the heavenly domain, so it is the most opposite in meaning. (Terrestrial / worldly / mundane are the standard dictionary antonyms of celestial.)

optionFeedback.html: "Heavenly" means of or like the heavens — it is a synonym of celestial, not its opposite. Picking it confuses a synonym with an antonym.
"Divine" means godlike or sacred, which matches the heavenly sense of celestial rather than reversing it; it is a synonym, so it cannot be the antonym.
"Supernatural" means beyond the natural / otherworldly, which is close in sense to celestial, not opposite to it — another synonym trap.
"Earthly" means belonging to the earth, worldly and terrestrial — it directly reverses the heavenly domain of celestial, which is exactly what an antonym requires.

title: Choose the word that roughly means the same as the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that most nearly means the same as the highlighted word in the sentence below.

Students who prepare for their board exams shouldn't neglect the languages.
solution:
The highlighted word is "neglect," which means to fail to give proper care or attention to something that deserves it.

Among the options, "ignore" (to refuse to take notice of / disregard) is the closest in meaning. Standard thesauruses list ignore and disregard as direct synonyms of neglect.

"Abandon" (to desert completely) is too strong, "decline" means to refuse or to decrease, and "fail" means to be unsuccessful — none of these conveys the sense of under-attending. Hence, the correct answer is "ignore."

optionFeedback.html: "Abandon" means to give something up completely or to desert it for good. "Neglect" is milder — it means failing to give due care or attention, not walking away entirely — so this does not match.
"Decline" means to politely refuse, or to decrease in quality or quantity. Neither sense captures the idea of failing to pay attention to something, so it is not a synonym of "neglect" here.

"Fail" means to be unsuccessful or to fall short of a goal. While you can "fail to do" something, the single word "fail" does not by itself mean to disregard or under-attend, so it is not the closest match.
"Ignore" means to refuse to take notice of, or to disregard, something. This matches "neglect," which means to fail to give proper attention or care — making it the closest synonym in this sentence.

title: From the option given below, choose the correct synonym which
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
From the options given below, choose the correct synonym which is the nearest in meaning to:

Parsimonious
solution:
Concept

A synonym is a word that carries the same or nearly the same meaning as another word. To pick the nearest synonym, fix the core meaning of the key word first, then match it against each choice by sense, and watch out for antonyms, which mean the opposite.

Application

"Parsimonious" describes someone who is excessively unwilling to spend money or resources, that is, miserly, stingy, or frugal to a fault. The needed word must express this same idea of extreme tight-fistedness.

"Penurious" carries exactly this sense: extremely sparing or stingy with money, and by extension extremely poor. It matches the core meaning of being unwilling to spend.

Contrast

  • Pessimistic: expecting the worst outcome; about a gloomy outlook, not about spending money.

  • Generous: freely giving and open-handed; this is the opposite of being tight with money.

  • Despondent: in low spirits, dejected; an emotional state, unrelated to thriftiness.

Only "Penurious" shares the meaning of extreme miserliness, so it is the nearest synonym of "Parsimonious".

optionFeedback.html: Pessimistic means inclined to expect the worst or to dwell on the gloomy side of situations. It describes a person's outlook, so its sense is different from that of Parsimonious.

Penurious means extremely sparing with money, stingy and tight-fisted, and by extension very poor. It carries the same sense of excessive reluctance to spend that Parsimonious does, which makes the two words synonyms.
Generous means giving freely and readily, open-handed with money or help. Its sense runs opposite to that of Parsimonious, so it is an antonym rather than a synonym.
Despondent means low in spirits, dejected, or in despair. It describes an emotional state, so its sense is different from that of Parsimonious.

title: From the option given below, choose the correct synonym which
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
From the option given below, choose the correct synonym which is the nearest in meaning:

Persistence
solution:
Concept

A synonym is the word that is nearest in meaning to a given headword. Persistence denotes the quality of continuing firmly and steadily in a course of action, a purpose, or a state, especially in spite of difficulty, opposition, or discouragement.

Application

We need the option that conveys this same idea of steadfast, unyielding continuation of effort. Perseverance means exactly that: continued, determined effort to do or achieve something despite obstacles. It maps directly onto the sense of Persistence, so it is the nearest synonym.

Contrast with the other choices

  • Surcease — a cessation or bringing to an end; this expresses stopping, the opposite of continuing.

  • Interruption — a break or temporary halt in something; again the idea of stopping, not of sustained effort.

  • Accuracy — correctness or precision; a quality about being error-free, unrelated to continuing an effort.

optionFeedback.html: Surcease denotes a stopping or coming to an end of an action or process.
Interruption denotes a break or temporary halt during an ongoing activity.
Perseverance denotes continued, determined effort to keep going despite difficulty or obstacles.
Accuracy denotes correctness or precision — being free from error.

title: From the options given below, choose the correct antonym which
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
From the options given below, choose the correct antonym which is the most opposite in meaning:

Demur
solution:
Concept:

An antonym is the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word. The verb "demur" means to raise an objection, to hesitate, or to express reluctance or disagreement before accepting something. So its strongest antonym is a word that means to accept or consent to something willingly.

Application:

To demur is to push back or withhold agreement. The exact opposite action is to give one's agreement or sanction — "approve". Where demur signals "I object / I hold back", approve signals "I accept / I consent". This direct reversal of the action makes "approve" the most opposite in meaning.

Contrast with the other choices:

  • "Reject" — this means to refuse or turn down, which is close in spirit to objecting; it points in the SAME direction as demur, not opposite to it.

  • "Entrust" — this means to give someone responsibility or to hand something over for safekeeping; it is unrelated to agreeing or objecting.

  • "Allot" — this means to allocate or assign a share; it is about distribution, not about consent or objection.

Cross-check: replacing demur with its opposite in a sentence — "She did not demur" carries the same sense as "She approved" — confirms that approve is the correct antonym.

optionFeedback.html: "Reject" means to refuse or turn down. That is close to the meaning of demur (to object), so it lies in the same direction rather than being its opposite — a common trap when a distractor looks like a strong, decisive word.

"Entrust" means to place something in someone's care or to give them responsibility for it. Its meaning lies entirely in the area of handing over duties, not in expressing or withholding an opinion the way demur does, so it is unrelated to the meaning being tested.

"Allot" means to allocate or assign a portion or share of something. It belongs to the idea of dividing and distributing, which has nothing to do with the act of demurring, so it does not fit as the word being asked for.

"Approve" means to accept or sanction something willingly — the exact reversal of demur, which is to object or hold back. This direct opposition in the action of accepting versus objecting makes it the most opposite in meaning.

title: From the options given below, choose the correct antonym which
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
From the options given below, choose the correct antonym which is the most opposite in meaning:

Repulsive
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word that carries the OPPOSITE meaning of the given word. To find the most opposite, first fix the precise sense of the key word, then choose the option whose meaning sits at the other end of that scale — not merely a different word, and never a synonym.

Application

The word “Repulsive” means causing strong dislike or disgust — something that drives people away. Its true opposite must draw people in, i.e. cause liking or appeal. “Attractive” means pleasing and capable of drawing interest or admiration, which is exactly the reverse of driving people away — so it is the most opposite in meaning.

Contrast with the other choices

  • Repugnant — means highly distasteful or offensive; a synonym of the key word, not its opposite.

  • Revolting — means causing disgust or nausea; again a synonym, reinforcing the same sense rather than reversing it.

  • Incompatible — means unable to exist or work together; it describes mismatch, an idea unrelated to disgust, so neither opposite nor related.

optionFeedback.html: “Incompatible” means unable to exist or work together harmoniously. That is about mismatch between things, unrelated to the like/dislike scale, so it cannot be the opposite of a word meaning ‘disgusting’.
“Repugnant” means extremely distasteful or offensive. It expresses the SAME idea of disgust as the key word, so it is a synonym, not an antonym.

“Attractive” means pleasing and able to draw interest or admiration. It belongs to the liking end of the like/dislike scale, the side that draws people in — the reverse of a word meaning ‘driving people away in disgust’.
“Revolting” means causing disgust or nausea. This echoes the meaning of the key word rather than reversing it, so it is a synonym and cannot be the antonym.

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the underlined word. If you abstain from unnecessary criticism, you will be happier in life.
solution:
Concept

The verb ‘abstain’ means to deliberately hold back from doing something — to voluntarily refrain from or keep away from an action, often one that is tempting or easy to slip into. To choose the best synonym, look for the option that carries this same core idea: refraining from or keeping away from an act.

Applying it here

In ‘abstain from unnecessary criticism’, the sentence urges you to refrain from criticising needlessly. ‘Avoid’ means to keep away from or refrain from something, so replacing the word gives ‘avoid unnecessary criticism’, which keeps the meaning of the sentence intact. So ‘Avoid’ is the word that best expresses the meaning of ‘abstain’.

Why the other words do not fit

  • ‘Indulge’ means to give in to or freely take part in something — the very opposite of holding back.

  • ‘Differ’ means to be unlike something or to disagree with someone; it is about contrast, not refraining from an act.

  • ‘Deny’ means to declare something untrue or to refuse to grant a request; it is about rejecting a claim, not voluntarily keeping away from an activity.

optionFeedback.html: ‘Avoid’ means to keep away from or refrain from an action, which is exactly the sense of ‘abstain from’ — to deliberately hold back. ‘Avoid unnecessary criticism’ carries the same meaning as the original sentence.

‘Indulge’ means to give in to a desire and freely take part in something. Put into the sentence — ‘indulge in unnecessary criticism’ — it advises doing more of the criticism, which clashes with the rest of the sentence about being happier, so ‘indulge’ does not fit.
‘Differ’ means to be unlike something or to disagree with someone. ‘Differ from unnecessary criticism’ is not idiomatic English and gives no clear meaning in this sentence, so ‘differ’ does not fit.

‘Deny’ means to declare something untrue or to refuse a request. ‘Deny unnecessary criticism’ would mean rejecting or disproving the criticism rather than the action the sentence describes, so ‘deny’ does not fit.

title: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it. ELEGANT
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is the direct opposite of another word. The word “Elegant” describes something graceful, refined, and stylish in appearance, movement, or manner.

Application

The word that conveys the reverse of grace and refinement is “Awkward”, which means clumsy, ungainly, and lacking in grace.

Contrast

  • Natural — means unforced or unaffected, which is close in spirit to elegant rather than its opposite.

  • Neat — means tidy and orderly, a near-synonym of elegant, not its opposite.

  • Tactless — means lacking sensitivity in dealing with others, the opposite of “diplomatic”, not of “elegant”.

Result

Therefore, the opposite of “Elegant” is “Awkward”.

optionFeedback.html: “Natural” means unforced, unaffected, or occurring in nature; an elegant manner is often described as natural, so this word sits alongside elegant rather than against it.
“Neat” means clean, tidy, and well-ordered, which is close in sense to elegant; it is a near-synonym, not an opposite.
“Tactless” means lacking sensitivity or diplomacy in dealing with people; it is the opposite of “tactful”, and it concerns social manner rather than grace of form or style.
“Awkward” means clumsy, ungainly, and lacking grace, which directly reverses the graceful, refined sense of “Elegant”.

title: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word.

INNOCENT
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word that carries the opposite meaning of a given word. The task here is to find the word whose meaning is directly contrary to INNOCENT. INNOCENT describes a person who is free from guilt, blame, or wrongdoing — someone who has not committed an offence.

Application

The exact opposite of being free from blame is being responsible for an offence or wrongdoing. The word that names this is “Guilty”, which means having committed a crime or being at fault. Therefore Guilty is the antonym of INNOCENT.

Contrast with the other choices

  • “Naive” means lacking experience or worldly wisdom — this is close in sense to innocent, not opposite to it.

  • “Unfamiliar” means not known or not recognised; it is unrelated to the idea of guilt or blamelessness, so it is not an antonym.

  • “Childlike” means having the trusting, simple qualities of a child — again similar in tone to innocent rather than its opposite.

optionFeedback.html: “Naive” describes someone simple and lacking experience, which is a quality close in meaning to innocent rather than its reverse. An antonym must express the contrary idea, so a near-synonym cannot be correct.
“Unfamiliar” means not known or not recognised. It deals with how well something is known and has nothing to do with blame or blamelessness, so it is not the opposite of innocent.
“Childlike” means having the trusting, simple nature of a child. This sense is similar to innocent, not contrary to it, so it cannot be the required antonym.

“Guilty” means responsible for an offence or wrongdoing. This meaning is the exact reverse of being free from blame, which is precisely the contrary sense the question asks for as the opposite of innocent.

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the underlined word. A corrupt officer is a disgrace to the whole department.
solution:
Concept

A synonym question asks for the word whose meaning is closest to the target word in the given sense. The underlined word "disgrace" (as a noun) means the loss of honour or respect that results from dishonourable conduct — in short, a state of dishonour or shame. To answer, match this core sense, not merely a loosely related idea.

Application

In the sentence, "A corrupt officer is a disgrace to the whole department," the corrupt officer brings dishonour upon the department — the department is shamed by the officer's conduct. The word that carries this exact sense of dishonour/loss-of-respect is "shame."

Contrast

  • Disgust — a feeling of strong revulsion or distaste; it describes an emotional reaction, not loss of honour.

  • Disturbance — an interruption of order or calm (a commotion); unrelated to dishonour.

  • Scandal — a publicised incident of wrongdoing that causes outrage; it names an event, whereas "disgrace" names the resulting state of dishonour.

  • Shame — dishonour and loss of respect; this matches the core sense of "disgrace" exactly.

Therefore the word that best expresses the meaning of "disgrace" is "shame."

optionFeedback.html: "Disgust" names a feeling of strong revulsion or distaste. That is an emotional reaction to something offensive, not the loss of honour or respect that "disgrace" denotes, so it does not match the underlined word's meaning.
"Disturbance" means an interruption of order or calm — a commotion or unrest. It has no connection to dishonour or loss of reputation, so it is not a synonym of "disgrace."

"Scandal" refers to a publicised incident of wrongdoing that provokes outrage. It names an event, not the resulting state of lost honour that "disgrace" describes; choosing it confuses the triggering event with the condition the word denotes.
"Shame" means dishonour and the loss of respect that follows discreditable conduct — exactly the sense carried by "disgrace" in describing how a corrupt officer dishonours the whole department.

title: Select the ANTONYM of the given word. FINITE
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the ANTONYM of the given word.
FINITE
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is the opposite of another word. To find an antonym, fix the core meaning of the given word and look for the option that reverses it.

"Finite" means having limits or bounds — something that can be counted or measured and that comes to an end.

Applying it here

The opposite of "having limits / coming to an end" is "having no limits / never ending." Among the choices, the word that carries this meaning of being without bound is "Endless," which means infinite or limitless. So "Endless" is the antonym of "Finite."

Why the other choices do not fit

  • "Limited" — this is a synonym of "finite" (also means bounded/restricted), so it has the same sense, not the opposite.

  • "Deep" — refers to extent downward or intensity; it is unrelated to the idea of limit versus limitlessness.

  • "Wide" — refers to breadth or extent across; it too is unrelated to whether something has an end.

Cross-check: "finite" and "endless/infinite" are a standard antonym pair (finite ↔ infinite), confirming the choice.

optionFeedback.html: "Limited" means bounded or restricted, which is the same sense as "finite," not its opposite. This choice confuses a synonym with an antonym.
"Deep" describes extent downward or intensity. It has no bearing on whether something is bounded or unbounded, so it is not an opposite of "finite."
"Endless" means without limit or end, describing something that never stops. This sense is the direct reverse of "finite," which means bounded and ending.
"Wide" describes breadth or extent across. It does not address the idea of having or lacking an end, so it cannot be the opposite of "finite."

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the underlined word. He made some very pertinent comments. They would certainly help us revise the project.
solution:
Concept: In a synonym question you choose the option whose meaning is closest to the target word in the given context. The word ‘pertinent’ describes something that applies to and bears directly on the matter being discussed — to the point and materially useful.

Application: The sentence says the remarks ‘would certainly help us revise the project.’ A remark that genuinely helps revise the work must apply directly to it. The single word that names this quality — applicable to and bearing on the subject — is ‘Relevant’, the standard dictionary equivalent of ‘pertinent’.

Why the other words fall short:

  • ‘Thoughtful’ describes the care or reflection behind a remark — a quality of the speaker, not of its bearing on the topic.

  • ‘Applied’ means put to practical use; it speaks to how something is used, not to its meaning.

  • ‘Related’ conveys only a loose, general association, weaker and vaguer than the precise force of ‘pertinent’.

Therefore the best synonym is ‘Relevant’.

optionFeedback.html: ‘Thoughtful’ means showing care, reflection, or consideration for others. It characterises the attitude or temperament behind what is said, describing the person rather than the substance of the remark.
‘Relevant’ means applicable to and bearing on the subject at hand — the established dictionary equivalent of ‘pertinent’.
‘Applied’ means put into practical use or directed toward a particular purpose; it describes how something is employed or implemented, a sense of utilisation rather than of meaning.
‘Related’ means merely associated or having some general connection; it expresses only a loose, broad link in which two things happen to be connected in some way.

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the given word: COHERENT
solution:
Concept

A synonym question asks for the option whose meaning is closest to the given word. "Coherent" describes something that is logically connected and internally consistent, so its parts hold together and follow one another sensibly.

Application

Applying this to the given word, the option that matches "logically connected and consistent" is "Logical". Something coherent is reasoned and orderly, which is exactly what "logical" conveys.

Contrast

  • "Affiliated" means connected through formal membership or association, not consistency of ideas, so it does not capture the meaning.

  • "Convincing" means persuasive or believable; a coherent argument is often convincing, but the two words describe different qualities (consistency versus persuasiveness).

  • "Rambling" means disconnected and wandering, which is the opposite of coherent, so it is an antonym rather than a synonym.

optionFeedback.html: "Logical" means reasoned, orderly and internally consistent, which is precisely the sense of "coherent" — ideas that connect and follow one another sensibly.

"Affiliated" means joined to a group through formal membership or association. It describes an external relationship between bodies, which is a different idea from what the given word expresses, so it is not its synonym.
"Convincing" means persuasive or able to make someone believe something. It judges the effect a thing has on an audience, not the quality the given word denotes, so the match is only superficial.
"Rambling" means speaking or writing at length in a confused, wandering way. It expresses the opposite quality to the given word, so it is an antonym and cannot be the synonym.

title: Choose the correct synonym (most nearest meaning). 'Docile'
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the correct synonym (the word nearest in meaning):

'Docile'
solution:
Concept

A synonym is a word that carries the same or nearly the same meaning as another word. To pick the best synonym, fix the core sense of the target word, then choose the option whose meaning matches that sense most closely, rejecting any option that is opposite or unrelated.

Application

The adjective 'docile' describes a person or animal that is easy to manage, teach, or control — quiet, obedient and yielding to the will of others. Its core sense is therefore 'readily controlled or obedient'.

'Submissive' means ready to yield to the authority or will of another, that is, obedient and compliant. This matches the core sense of 'docile' almost exactly, so it is the nearest synonym.

Contrast with the other words

  • 'Stubborn' means refusing to change one's mind or yield — this is the opposite of being easy to control, so it is an antonym, not a synonym.

  • 'Strong' refers to physical or mental power and has nothing to do with obedience, so it is unrelated.

  • 'Changeable' means likely to vary or fluctuate, which describes inconstancy rather than obedience, so it too is unrelated.

Hence the word nearest in meaning to 'docile' is 'submissive'.

optionFeedback.html: 'Submissive' means ready to yield to another's authority or will — obedient and compliant. The core sense of 'docile' is being easy to manage and obey, and 'submissive' carries that same sense of yielding to control.

'Stubborn' means refusing to yield or change one's mind. The core sense of 'docile' is being easy to manage; refusing to yield runs in the opposite direction, so this word points away from that sense.

'Strong' means having physical or mental power. The core sense of 'docile' concerns how readily someone is managed or led, which is a different idea from power, so this word belongs to a separate sense.
'Changeable' means liable to vary or fluctuate. The core sense of 'docile' concerns ease of being controlled, while changeability is about inconstancy, so this word belongs to a separate sense.

title: Choose the correct synonym (most nearest meaning). 'Bemoan'
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the correct synonym (most nearest meaning).

'Bemoan'
solution:
Concept

A synonym is a word that carries the most nearly the same meaning as the target word. To find it, fix the precise sense of the target word first, then match the option whose core meaning aligns with that sense — not merely a word from the same emotional area.

Application

The verb “bemoan” means to express grief, sorrow, or dissatisfaction about something — to mourn or wail over it aloud. The option that means “to express grief or sorrow about something” is Lament, which matches this sense exactly.

Contrast

  • Soothe — to calm, comfort, or relieve distress. This is the opposite movement: it eases sorrow rather than expressing it.

  • Denounce — to publicly condemn or accuse. It targets blame at a person or act, not personal grief.

  • Loathe — to feel intense dislike or disgust. It names an emotion of hatred, not the act of mourning or grieving.

Only Lament shares the core sense of voicing grief, so it is the nearest synonym of “bemoan.”

optionFeedback.html: “Lament” means to express grief or sorrow about something, which is exactly the sense of “bemoan” — to mourn or wail over a loss or hardship. The two words name the same act of voicing sorrow.
“Soothe” means to calm, comfort, or relieve distress. That is the reverse of “bemoan”: it eases sorrow instead of expressing it, so it cannot be a synonym.
“Denounce” means to publicly condemn or accuse someone or something. It directs blame outward rather than voicing personal grief, so it does not match “bemoan.”
“Loathe” means to feel intense dislike or disgust. It names an emotion of hatred toward something, not the act of mourning or grieving over it, so it misses the meaning of “bemoan.”

title: Choose the correct antonym (most opposite meaning). 'Gargantuan'
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the correct antonym (most opposite meaning).

'Gargantuan'
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is the most opposite to that of a given word. The task is not to find a related word, but the word that lies at the far end of the same scale of meaning. For size, that scale runs from extremely large at one end to extremely small at the other.

Application

'Gargantuan' means enormous, gigantic, immense — occupying the 'extremely large' end of the size scale (it comes from Gargantua, the giant in Rabelais's tales). Its most opposite meaning is therefore a word meaning 'extremely small'. 'Dwarf', used to describe something, means very small or stunted in size, which sits at the opposite extreme of the same scale.

Contrast with the near-misses

  • Colossal — means huge or vast; this is a synonym of gargantuan, not its opposite, so it is on the same end of the scale.

  • Humongo — from 'humongous', meaning extremely large; again a synonym of gargantuan, not an opposite.

  • Routinely — an adverb meaning 'as a regular habit'; it has nothing to do with size at all, so it cannot be an antonym of a size word.

Only 'Dwarf' expresses the opposite of large, so it is the correct antonym of 'Gargantuan'.

optionFeedback.html: 'Humongo', from 'humongous', means extremely large. That places its meaning at the large end of the size scale, the same end as gargantuan.
'Dwarf', describing something, means very small or stunted in size. That places its meaning at the small end of the size scale, the far end from gargantuan.
'Colossal' means huge or vast. That places its meaning at the large end of the size scale, the same end as gargantuan.
'Routinely' is an adverb meaning 'as a regular habit'. Its meaning lies on a scale of frequency, not of size, so it is off the size scale entirely.

title: Choose the correct antonym (most opposite meaning). 'Exposition'
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the correct antonym (most opposite meaning).

'Exposition'
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is the most directly opposite to that of a given word. To find one, first fix the precise sense of the target word, then look for the offered choice that denotes its reverse, not merely a related or similar idea.

Exposition means a comprehensive setting-forth, explaining, or making-known of an idea, theory, or material in detail (also a public display that puts things on show). Its essence is to reveal and explain openly.

Application

Test each choice against the sense “to set forth and explain openly”:

  • Explanation – to make something clear; this is the same idea as exposition, so it is a synonym, not an opposite.

  • Critique – a detailed evaluation or judgement of something; this is a related analytical act, not the reverse of explaining.

  • Pronouncement – a formal public declaration; this too involves making something known, so it sits on the same side as exposition.

  • Silence – the state of saying nothing, withholding explanation or expression; this is the direct reverse of setting forth and making known.

The word that reverses “open explanation/making-known” is Silence, because it denotes the complete absence of expounding or expression.

Cross-check

Standard thesauruses list “explanation” among the synonyms of exposition and place “silence” on the opposite side. So the choice that holds, Silence, is confirmed as the most opposite in meaning among the four.

optionFeedback.html: "Explanation" carries the same idea as setting forth and clarifying a matter, so it is a synonym of "exposition" rather than its opposite — picking it confuses a like-meaning word with an antonym.

"Critique" is a detailed assessment or judgement of a work; that is a related analytical activity, not the reverse of explaining or presenting something — it answers "what is your evaluation", not "the opposite of exposition".

"Silence" denotes saying nothing and withholding all expression or explanation, which is precisely the reverse of "exposition" (an open setting-forth and making-known). It is therefore the most opposite in meaning.
"Pronouncement" is a formal public declaration — still an act of making something known, the same direction as "exposition" — so it cannot be its opposite.

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

DEVOUR
solution:
Concept

A synonym question asks for the word closest in meaning to the given word. To solve it, fix the core sense of the headword, then test each candidate for the same core sense rather than a loose association.

Application

The headword "DEVOUR" means to eat or swallow up hungrily and completely; by extension it means to use up or take in entirely. Its core sense is therefore "to take in or use up completely".

Among the candidates, "Consume" carries exactly this core sense — to eat, drink, or use up entirely — so it matches DEVOUR most closely.

Contrast

  • Assign — means to allot a task or give out; it concerns distribution of duties, not eating or using up.

  • Despise — means to look down on or regard with contempt; it is an attitude of scorn, unrelated to the act of consuming.

  • Design — means to plan, sketch, or devise; it concerns creating a plan, the opposite of using something up.

Only "Consume" preserves the core sense of taking in or using up completely, so it is the best synonym for DEVOUR.

optionFeedback.html: "Assign" means to allot or hand out a task to someone. It describes giving out duties, a sense quite different from DEVOUR, so it is a poor match.
"Despise" means to scorn or look down on with contempt. It names an attitude of dislike, which does not line up with the meaning of DEVOUR.
"Consume" means to eat, drink, or use up entirely, which is the very sense DEVOUR carries, so it best expresses the meaning of the headword.
"Design" means to plan, sketch, or devise something. It points to creating a plan, a meaning unrelated to DEVOUR, so it does not fit.

title: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text: Select the word that best expresses the meaning of the given word. EXOTIC
solution:
Concept

A “best synonym” question asks for the option whose meaning is closest to the headword. The test is substitution: the right answer is the word that could replace the headword in a sentence while keeping the same sense, not merely a word that is loosely associated with it.

Application

The headword EXOTIC means strikingly different from the ordinary — strange, foreign, or not commonly seen. Its core sense is “out of the ordinary.” The option that carries this same meaning is Unusual, which directly denotes “not usual, uncommon, out of the ordinary.” It passes the substitution test: an “exotic plant” and an “unusual plant” both convey something uncommon.

Contrast

Checking the remaining choices against the meaning of “exotic”:

  • Familiar — means well-known and ordinary; this is the opposite of “exotic,” so it is an antonym, not a synonym.

  • Thorough — means complete or carried out in full detail; it describes effort or care, unrelated to strangeness or foreignness.

  • Excessive — means too much in amount or degree; it speaks to quantity, not to being unusual or foreign.

Only the choice meaning “out of the ordinary” matches “exotic,” which is why Unusual is correct.

optionFeedback.html: “Thorough” means complete or done in full detail — it describes how carefully an action is carried out. That is a comment on effort and completeness, a different kind of quality from the one the headword names, so it is not a match.

“Excessive” means more than is needed — it is a judgement about quantity or degree. The headword is not making a point about amount, so a word about “too much” answers a different question and does not fit.

“Familiar” means well-known, comfortable, and frequently encountered — it describes things we already know well. That everyday, comfortable sense is simply not the idea the headword expresses, so although it is a tempting single-word choice, its meaning does not line up with the headword’s.

“Unusual” means not usual, uncommon, out of the ordinary — and that is exactly the core sense the headword carries. It substitutes cleanly: “an exotic location” and “an unusual location” both point to something out of the ordinary.

title: Select the ANTONYM of the given word. COINCIDE
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the ANTONYM of the given word.
COINCIDE
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is opposite to that of a given word. To find an antonym, first fix the core sense of the target word, then choose the option that expresses the reverse of that sense — not merely a word that is unrelated or that begins with the same prefix.

“Coincide” means to agree, to correspond exactly, or to be in harmony (two opinions, accounts, or events that match each other).

Application

The reverse of “to agree / correspond” is “to differ in opinion / fail to correspond.” Among the choices, “Disagree” carries exactly this opposite sense — to hold a contrary view or to be at variance — so it is the true antonym of coincide.

Contrast

  • “Disappear” means to cease to be visible; it is the opposite of “appear,” not of “agree,” so it does not reverse the sense of coincide.

  • “Disappoint” means to fail to fulfil someone’s hopes; it concerns expectation, not agreement or correspondence.

  • “Disbelieve” means to refuse to accept as true; it is the opposite of “believe,” and has nothing to do with two things matching.

The “dis-” prefix on every choice is a deliberate trap: a shared prefix does not make a word an opposite. Only the option that reverses the meaning of “agree / correspond” qualifies.

optionFeedback.html: This is the opposite of “appear,” describing something that ceases to be visible. That sense concerns presence, not whether two opinions or accounts match, so it does not reverse the meaning of “coincide.”
This means to let someone down or fail their expectations. It deals with hopes being unmet, not with agreement or correspondence, so it is not the opposite of “coincide.”
This is the opposite of “believe” — to reject something as untrue. It is about trust in a claim, not about two things matching, so it does not capture the reverse of “coincide.”

“Disagree” means to hold a contrary opinion or to be at variance. Relative to “coincide,” which means to agree or correspond, this expresses the reverse of that core sense rather than mere irrelevance or a shared prefix.

title: Select the ANTONYM of the given word. LAVISH
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the ANTONYM of the given word.

LAVISH
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word whose meaning is opposite to that of a given word. To find one, first fix the precise sense of the cue word, then choose the option that expresses its direct opposite (not a synonym or an unrelated word).

"Lavish" means given, spent, or produced in large, generous, even excessive amounts — abundant and extravagant.

Application

The opposite of "abundant / extravagant" is something scanty and inadequate in quantity. "Meagre" means lacking in quantity or quality — sparse, scanty, deficient — which is the direct opposite of lavish. So the antonym is "Meagre".

Contrast with the other words

  • "Laudable" means deserving praise; it describes worth, not amount, so it is unrelated to the abundant/scanty axis.

  • "Liberal" means generous and free in giving — this is a synonym of lavish, not its opposite.

  • "Excessive" means more than what is needed or proper — again close in sense to lavish, not opposite to it.

optionFeedback.html: "Laudable" means worthy of praise. It expresses approval of something's merit or admirable quality, and has no opposing connection to the idea of extravagant abundance carried by "lavish", so it cannot serve as its antonym.

"Meagre" means scanty, sparse and insufficient in amount — the direct reverse of being given or produced in generous, extravagant quantity. That opposition in degree of quantity is exactly what an antonym of "lavish" requires.
"Liberal" means generous and unstinting in giving. That is the same idea as "lavish", so it is a synonym — picking it inverts the task of finding an opposite.
"Excessive" means going beyond what is needed or appropriate. This stays on the side of "too much", echoing "lavish" rather than reversing it, so it is a near-synonym, not an antonym.

title: Select the ANTONYM of the given word. OPPRESSIVE
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Select the ANTONYM of the given word.
OPPRESSIVE
solution:
Concept

An antonym is a word that expresses the opposite meaning of another word. To find the antonym of a word, first fix its core meaning, then look for the option whose meaning directly reverses it. Oppressive describes something cruel, harsh, and unjustly burdensome — typically the behaviour of a tyrannical authority that crushes people. Its opposite is therefore a quality of kindness, mercy and compassion toward people.

Application

The core sense of oppressive is "cruel and merciless toward people." The word that directly reverses this sense is humane, which means "marked by compassion, sympathy and consideration for people." Treating people humanely is the exact opposite of treating them oppressively, so humane is the antonym.

Contrast with the other choices

  • Voluntary means "done of one's own free will." Its true opposite is "compulsory/forced," so it does not reverse the cruelty sense of oppressive.

  • Wise means "having good judgement." Its opposite is "foolish"; it is unrelated to the harshness sense of oppressive.

  • Prosperous means "flourishing or wealthy." Its opposite is "poor/unsuccessful"; it describes financial condition, not treatment of people.

Antonym = Humane.

optionFeedback.html: "Voluntary" means done by free choice. Its meaningful opposite is "compulsory" or "forced," which sits on the free-will axis. That axis is not the one the given word belongs to, so its opposite cannot be the answer here.
"Wise" means having sound judgement. Its opposite is "foolish," which lies on the judgement axis. The given word is not about quality of judgement, so this word's opposite does not match.
"Humane" means kind, compassionate and merciful toward people. This meaning directly reverses cruel, harsh and merciless treatment, which is what the given word describes.

"Prosperous" means flourishing or wealthy. Its opposite is "poor" or "unsuccessful," which describes financial condition. The given word is not about wealth, so this word's opposite is on the wrong axis.

title: Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted word in the sentence.

The supervisor was asked to slacken the pace of work as there was no immediate hurry.
solution:
CONCEPT

An antonym question asks for the word whose meaning directly reverses the highlighted word's sense — not a related word or a synonym. First pin down the exact sense the highlighted word carries in this sentence, then match that sense's precise opposite.

APPLICATION

Here, "slacken" means to make something slower, looser, or less active; in this sentence it means to reduce the pace of work. The direct opposite of reducing pace is increasing it, i.e. to speed up or hasten. This is exactly what "accelerate" means, so it reverses "slacken" in this context.

CROSS-CHECK / CONTRAST

Checking the other options confirms none of them reverse the sense of slowing down:

  • "monitor" means to watch or keep track of an activity; it describes observation, not a change in speed, so it does not oppose "slacken".

  • "supervise" means to oversee or direct work, again a managerial role, not a reversal of pace.

  • "control" means to regulate or restrain the pace; this sits closer to moderating/slowing than to speeding up, so it does not reverse "slacken" either.

Result: since only one option reverses the "reduce pace" sense of "slacken" into "increase pace," that option is the correct antonym.

optionFeedback.html: "Monitor" means to watch or keep track of something — an act of observation. This meaning does not reverse what "slacken" expresses in the sentence, so it is not the antonym here.
"Accelerate" means to increase speed or hasten progress; it directly reverses the sense of reducing pace carried by "slacken" in this sentence.
"Supervise" means to direct or oversee work — a managerial role. This meaning does not reverse what "slacken" expresses in the sentence, so it is not the antonym here.
"Control" means to regulate or restrain something. This stays within the same broad direction as "slacken" rather than reversing it, so it is not the antonym here.

title: Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
text:
Choose the word that means the opposite of the highlighted word in the sentence.

Rohit's analysis of the poem is profound.
solution:
CONCEPT

An antonym question asks for the word whose meaning directly reverses the highlighted word's sense in this exact context, not merely a dissimilar or generically negative word. First pin down the precise sense the highlighted word carries here, then match that sense's exact opposite.

APPLICATION
