Therefore, while technology offers numerous advantages, it must be used responsibly and in moderation to ensure a balanced and meaningful life.

The internet has reduced ____.
solution:
Concept: A literal-comprehension question asks you to locate information that the passage states directly, in its own words, rather than requiring you to infer, generalise, or bring in outside knowledge. The correct choice must correspond, word for word or in close paraphrase, to a specific clause in the passage.

Application: The passage states: "The internet has made it possible for individuals to connect instantly across different parts of the world, thereby reducing geographical barriers." This sentence directly names what the internet has reduced, so the blank must be filled with that value.

Contrast with the other options:

  • educational opportunities — the passage says institutions increasingly rely on digital platforms to provide learning opportunities, which describes greater use of such platforms, not a reduction in educational opportunities.

  • business activities — the passage says businesses use technology to improve efficiency and productivity, which describes an improvement, not a reduction in business activities.

  • social awareness — the passage never makes any claim about social awareness; it discusses reduced face-to-face interaction and data-privacy concerns instead.

Cross-check: Re-reading the sentence confirms that reducing geographical barriers is the only reduction the passage explicitly attributes to the internet, which matches the value in that option.

optionFeedback.html: Educational opportunities refers to access to learning resources, courses, or institutional support available to students.
Geographical barriers refers to distance- or location-based obstacles that make direct interaction between people in different places difficult.
Business activities refers to the commercial operations and processes organisations carry out to produce goods or deliver services.
Social awareness refers to an individual's understanding of and sensitivity to social issues, relationships, and community well-being.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q19
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Direction: Read the following passage carefully and choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below each question.

Passage: In recent years, the rapid advancement of technology has transformed the way people communicate, work and access information. The internet has made it possible for individuals to connect instantly across different parts of the world, thereby reducing geographical barriers. Educational institutions increasingly rely on digital platforms to provide learning opportunities, while businesses use technology to improve efficiency and productivity. However, excessive dependence on technology has also created several challenges, including reduced face-to-face interaction, concerns about data privacy, and increased levels of distraction among young people. Therefore, while technology offers numerous advantages, it must be used responsibly and in moderation to ensure a balanced and meaningful life.

Why do businesses use technology ?
solution:
Concept: In a passage-based comprehension question that asks why something happened, the correct option is the one that directly restates the reason the passage itself gives for that action, not an option that reverses the stated direction, borrows a detail from an unrelated part of the passage, or introduces information the passage never mentions.

Application: The passage states, "businesses use technology to improve efficiency and productivity." This sentence directly names the reason: to improve efficiency and productivity.

Cross-check: Contrasting each option against the passage:

  • "to reduce productivity" reverses the direction the passage states; the passage says technology is used to improve, not reduce, productivity.

  • "to avoid communication" borrows from an earlier, unrelated part of the passage, where the internet is described as helping individuals connect instantly, not as a reason businesses use technology.

  • "to increase manual work" is never mentioned in the passage and runs counter to its overall theme of technology improving efficiency.

Result: The passage's own stated reason, to improve efficiency and productivity, is the answer.

optionFeedback.html: This describes an operational-output action: reducing productivity, that is, lowering the ratio of output produced per unit of input.
This describes an interpersonal-interaction action: avoiding communication, that is, choosing not to engage in information exchange with others.
This describes an operational-output action: improving efficiency and productivity, that is, raising the ratio of output produced per unit of input.
This describes an operational-method action: increasing manual work, that is, raising the proportion of tasks performed by hand rather than by machine.

title: TPSC Junior Forensic Digital Analyst 2026 Q20
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Direction: Read the following passage carefully and choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below each question.

Passage: In recent years, the rapid advancement of technology has transformed the way people communicate, work and access information. The internet has made it possible for individuals to connect instantly across different parts of the world, thereby reducing geographical barriers. Educational institutions increasingly rely on digital platforms to provide learning opportunities, while businesses use technology to improve efficiency and productivity. Therefore, while technology offers numerous advantages, it must be used responsibly and in moderation to ensure a balanced and meaningful life.

According to the passage, technology should be used ____.
solution:
Concept: A literal-comprehension question asks what the passage explicitly states about a term or idea, not what can be inferred beyond the text. The correct choice is the option whose wording most closely reproduces the passage's own stated conclusion, without adding, removing, or softening its qualifiers.

Application: The passage's closing sentence states: "Therefore, while technology offers numerous advantages, it must be used responsibly and in moderation to ensure a balanced and meaningful life." This sentence attaches two qualifiers — responsibility and moderation — to technology's use, and those two words appear together in one of the four options.

  • "responsibly and in moderation": The passage's final sentence states that technology "must be used responsibly and in moderation to ensure a balanced and meaningful life."

  • "without limitations": The passage states that "excessive dependence on technology has also created several challenges, including reduced face-to-face interaction, concerns about data privacy, and increased levels of distraction among young people."

  • "only for entertainment": The passage names technology's roles as enabling instant communication across the world, providing learning opportunities through digital platforms, and improving business efficiency and productivity; entertainment is not among the roles named.

  • "only in educational institutions": The passage states that "educational institutions increasingly rely on digital platforms to provide learning opportunities, while businesses use technology to improve efficiency and productivity," describing technology's use across both education and business, not institutions alone.

Cross-check: Scanning the passage's stated conclusion for each option's exact wording shows only one option reproducing both qualifiers named there — "responsibly and in moderation" — while the others introduce a scope (unlimited use, entertainment only, institutions only) the passage's conclusion does not state.

optionFeedback.html: The qualifier this phrase adds to technology's use, stated plainly: responsibly, in moderation.
The qualifier this phrase adds to technology's use, stated plainly: without limitations.
The qualifier this phrase adds to technology's use, stated plainly: only for entertainment.
The qualifier this phrase adds to technology's use, stated plainly: only in educational institutions.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q94
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and select the correct option.

We planned to travel Calcutta towards the end of last November. We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week. It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky. We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air. The hostess brought water bottle for each passenger along with a light meal packet in a card board box. She also served tea or coffee according to the demands of the passengers. One passenger asked her when to open the box. She replied, ‘you can take it now or keep it to be used later’. We did not open the box then and there as we did not feel any urge for we just took our meals.

The journey began in November in the
solution:
A detail question in a comprehension passage is answered by locating the exact fact, time, or place stated in the passage itself, not by outside assumption or general impression. When the passage names a specific ordinal marker such as a day or week, that stated marker is the answer.

The passage states: ‘We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week.’ This sentence explicitly places the start of the journey on the third day of the fourth week. Since the opening line places the trip ‘towards the end of last November’, this fourth week falls within November.

  • 1st week: not supported — the passage does not describe the journey beginning in the first week.

  • 2nd week: not supported — the passage does not place the journey in the second week.

  • 3rd week: not supported — the passage specifies the fourth week, not the third.

  • 4th week: matches the passage’s explicit statement, ‘the third day of the fourth week.’

Therefore, the journey began in the 4th week of November.

optionFeedback.html: In a standard four-week division of a month, this option's week spans days 1 to 7.
In a standard four-week division of a month, this option's week spans days 8 to 14.
In a standard four-week division of a month, this option's week spans days 15 to 21.
In a standard four-week division of a month, this option's week spans days 22 to 28.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q95
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and select the correct option.

We planned to travel to Calcutta towards the end of last November. We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long-cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week. It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky. We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air. The hostess brought a water bottle for each passenger along with a light meal packet in a card-board box. She also served tea or coffee according to the demands of the passengers. One passenger asked her when to open the box. She replied, ‘you can take it now or keep it to be used later’. We did not open the box then and there, as we did not feel any urge for it since we had just taken our meals.

The passage refers to a journey
solution:
Concept: A literal-comprehension question asks you to identify a fact that is directly stated or clearly implied by the passage's own wording, without needing any outside knowledge — the answer is found by locating the descriptive clues the passage itself supplies for the mode of travel, the crew, and the physical sensations described.

  1. Locate the clue describing the vehicle's motion: the passage states, "We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air" — a vehicle moving "into the air" describes an ascent off the ground.

  2. Locate the clue describing the crew: the passage refers to the attendant as "the hostess," a term describing cabin crew who serve refreshments to seated passengers.

  3. Combine both clues: an ascent "into the air" together with a "hostess" serving water and a meal packet in a card-board box to seated passengers matches a mode of travel where passengers are airborne and served by cabin crew during the journey.

Contrast with the other options, each ruled out by the same clues:

  • by train — a train stays on the ground on rail tracks; it does not "move into the air," so the ascent clue does not fit this mode.

  • by ship — a ship stays on the surface of the water; it does not "move into the air" either, so the ascent clue rules this mode out too.

  • by bus — a bus travels on roads at ground level; "moved smoothly into the air" does not describe road travel.

Result: the only mode of travel consistent with a vehicle that "moved smoothly into the air" and an attendant called "the hostess" is by air.

optionFeedback.html: A train journey typically takes place in compartments arranged along rail tracks, staff are usually referred to as conductors or ticket examiners, and the ride is felt as motion along the ground.
A sea voyage typically takes place aboard a vessel with cabins and decks, crew members are usually referred to as stewards or pursers, and the journey is felt as motion across water.
A road journey by bus typically takes place in seats arranged along a highway route, staff are usually referred to as conductors, and the ride is felt as motion along paved roads.
An air journey typically takes place aboard an aircraft with cabin crew usually referred to as hostesses or flight attendants, and the vehicle ascends off the ground into the sky.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q96
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and select the correct option.

We planned to travel Calcutta towards the end of last November. We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week. It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky. We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air. The hostess brought water bottle for each passenger along with a light meal packet in a card board box. She also served tea or coffee according to the demands of the passengers. One passenger asked her when to open the box. She replied, ‘you can take it now or keep it to be used later’. We did not open the box then and there as we did not feel any urge for we just took our meals.

The weather on the day of journey was
solution:
Concept: In literal (detail-based) reading comprehension, the correct option is the one that directly restates a fact stated in the passage itself, without requiring any inference beyond the given words.

Application: The passage states, "It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky." This sentence directly describes the atmospheric conditions on the day of the journey: a clear sky, sunshine, and no clouds. The everyday English word for this kind of weather is "fair".

Cross-check:

  • foul — describes weather marked by storms, rain, or strong wind; the passage's "very clear day without a cloud" rules this description out.

  • stormy — describes weather marked by strong wind, heavy rain, and thunder; contradicted by the passage's "very clear day."

  • fair — describes weather marked by a clear sky and sunshine with no clouds or rain; this matches "a very clear day without a cloud in the sky" exactly.

  • cloudy — describes weather marked by significant cloud cover across the sky; directly contradicted by the passage's "without a cloud in the sky."

Result: Only "fair" matches the passage's own description of the day, so "fair" is the correct answer.

optionFeedback.html: "Foul weather" refers to atmospheric conditions marked by strong wind, rain, or storm activity that disrupt outdoor movement.
"Stormy weather" refers to atmospheric conditions marked by strong wind, heavy rain, thunder, and lightning occurring together.
"Fair weather" refers to atmospheric conditions marked by a clear sky, sunshine, and calm, settled air with no rain.
"Cloudy weather" refers to atmospheric conditions marked by extensive cloud cover across the sky, often limiting direct sunlight.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q99
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and select the correct option.

We planned to travel Calcutta towards the end of last November. We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week. It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky. We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air. The hostess brought water bottle for each passenger along with a light meal packet in a card board box. She also served tea or coffee according to the demands of the passengers. One passenger asked her when to open the box. She replied, ‘you can take it now or keep it to be used later’. We did not open the box then and there as we did not feel any urge for we just took our meals.

Passengers were asked to eat the food
solution:
Literal, detail-based reading comprehension questions are answered by locating the exact sentence in the passage that addresses the question and matching its stated meaning to the option that expresses the same idea in full, without adding or dropping any part of what was said.

In the passage, when a passenger asked the hostess when to open the box, she replied, “you can take it now or keep it to be used later.” This single sentence explicitly offers two alternatives for the timing of eating the meal, consuming it right away, or delaying it, and leaves the choice to the passenger.

Checking each timing phrase against this reply: a phrase that names only immediate consumption captures half of what was said, and a phrase that names only delayed consumption captures the other half; a phrase combining both timings mirrors the hostess's reply in full, while a phrase about disposing of the food does not appear in the reply at all.

optionFeedback.html: This phrase denotes consuming the meal packet without any delay, as soon as it is received.
This phrase denotes deferring consumption of the meal packet to a subsequent, unspecified time.
This phrase denotes leaving the choice of timing open, permitting consumption either right away or after a delay.
This phrase denotes disposing of the meal packet rather than consuming it.

title: TPSC Sub Inspector Excise 2014 Q100
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and select the correct option.

We planned to travel Calcutta towards the end of last November. We arranged tickets for the journey from an agency and began our long cherished journey on the third day of the fourth week. It was a very clear day without a cloud in the sky. We felt very little motion as the vehicle moved smoothly into the air. The hostess brought water bottle for each passenger along with a light meal packet in a card board box. She also served tea or coffee according to the demands of the passengers. One passenger asked her when to open the box. She replied, ‘you can take it now or keep it to be used later’. We did not open the box then and there as we did not feel any urge for we just took our meals.

We did not open the box as

options.html: we wanted to leave the food behind
we wanted to donate the food to someone

solution:
A reading-comprehension 'reason' question is answered by matching the stem to the exact justification given in the passage itself — a choice must be confirmed by what the text actually states, not by any generally plausible reason for the character's behaviour.

The passage gives the reason directly: ‘We did not open the box then and there as we did not feel any urge for we just took our meals.’ Having just had their meals, the passengers felt no pressing need to open the box right away — that is, there was no immediate demand for its contents.

  • 'We wanted to leave the food behind' would mean a decision to abandon the meal for good; the passage describes only a delay in opening the box, never an intention to discard it.

  • 'We wanted to donate the food to someone' would require an intention to give the food away to another person; no such plan is mentioned anywhere in the passage.

  • 'The food was not good' would be a judgement on the meal's quality; the passage makes no comment at all about taste or quality.

Since the passage's own stated reason is the absence of any pressing need at that moment, the passage-supported answer is 'there was no immediate demand.'

optionFeedback.html: This phrasing describes a general absence of urgency at a given moment — a state in which nothing pressing requires immediate action right then.
This phrasing describes a deliberate decision to abandon or forgo an item altogether, implying permanent non-use of it going forward.
This phrasing describes an intention to hand something over to another person, implying a specific plan to redistribute it rather than to keep or consume it personally.
This phrasing describes a quality judgement about an item, attributing an action to a defect or lack of appeal in the item itself.

title: UPPSC Computer Operator Grade B — 2021 — Q83
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage carefully and select the correct answer to the questions given at the end of the passage.

Ecosystems provide people with a variety of goods and services, such as food, clean water, clean air, flood control, soil stabilization, pollination, climate regulation, spiritual fulfillment and aesthetic enjoyment, to name just a few. Most of these benefits are either irreplaceable or the technology necessary to replace them is prohibitively expensive. For example potable fresh water can be extracted by desalinating sea water, but only at great cost.

The rapidly expanding human population has greatly modified the earth’s ecosystem to meet their increased requirements of some goods and services, particularly food, fresh water, timber, fibre and fuel. These modifications have contributed substantially to human well being and economic development. The benefits have not been equally distributed.

Some people have actually been harmed by these changes. Moreover, short-term increases in some ecosystems’ goods and services have come at the cost of long term degradation of others. For example, efforts to increase the production of food and fibre have decreased the ability of some ecosystems to provide clean water, regulate flooding and support biodiversity.

Which of the following can be considered as the most suitable title for the passage?
solution:
Concept

A suitable title expresses a passage’s broad controlling idea, not a detail, example, or cause mentioned only briefly. The best method is to identify the subject repeated across the passage and the development of that subject from beginning to end.

A title should cover the passage as a whole: its opening focus, its main explanation, and its concluding consequence or contrast.

Application

The passage first explains the goods and services supplied by ecosystems. It then describes how growing human requirements have modified ecosystems, producing economic benefits but distributing them unevenly. Finally, it shows that short-term gains can cause long-term degradation of other ecosystem services.

Contrast

  • Food crisis: food appears as one of several demanded goods and as an example of production trade-offs; the passage does not describe a crisis of food availability.

  • Technological development: technology appears only in the desalination example, which illustrates the high cost of replacing an ecosystem service.

  • Population control: population growth is presented as a cause of increased demand, while population-control measures are not discussed.

  • Modification of our ecosystem: this phrase covers the passage’s full movement from ecosystem services to human alteration, benefits, unequal effects, and long-term degradation.

Cross-check and result

Checking each paragraph against the candidate title shows that ecosystem modification is the only idea that remains relevant throughout the passage. Therefore, the most suitable title is “Modification of our ecosystem.”

optionFeedback.html: The passage associates food with human demand and explains that increasing food and fibre production can reduce clean-water, flood-control, and biodiversity services.
The passage associates technology with desalination, which can supply potable fresh water by replacing an ecosystem service at high cost.
The passage associates population growth with increased requirements for food, fresh water, timber, fibre, and fuel.
The passage associates ecosystem modification with meeting human requirements and with economic benefits, unequal effects, and degradation of other ecosystem services.

title: Nothing is sure but death and taxes, and of course
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Nothing is sure but death and taxes, and of course that north is north and south is south, and thus it has always been, so they say. But they’d be wrong. You can perhaps be sure about death and taxes, but you might want to reconsider the rest of it. In fact, at many times in our planet’s history, north has become south and south has become north, in a process called magnetic reversal. Paleogeologists have discovered the existence of these mysterious phenomena (in a field study known as paleomagnetism) by investigating rocks. When rocks are being formed from magmas, atoms within their crystals respond to the earth’s magnetic field by “pointing” towards the magnetic alignment, scientists can determine where on earth the north pole was located at that time because as the rocks solidified, they trapped that information within them. The study of ancient lava flows has revealed that at certain periods in the earth’s history magnetic north was directly opposite to its present location. In fact, it has been determined that the north/south reversal has occurred on average every 500,000 years and that the last reversal took place about 700,000 years ago. Scientists call those periods of “normal” polarity (the magnetic orientation of our modern er(1) and “reversed” polarity (the magnetic orientation of reverse situation) by the name “magnetic chrons.” Although the fad : of such reversals is clear, why and how they happen and their effects on the planet are subjects of considerable debate. Because no one knows precisely how the earth’s magnetic field is produced, it becomes difficult so say how it might be reversed. Among explanations proposed are a reversal of the direction of convection currents in the liquid outer core of the earth and a collision between the earth and a meteorite or comet. And while the precise effects of a reversal are not known, there can be little doubt that the earth would receive during the process a great deal more damaging ultraviolet radiation than it now does and that such occurrences have been correlated with the extinction of certain species in the geologic past.

According to the passage, which of the following was crucial to the discovery of magnetic reversal?

options.html: The extinction of certain species 700,000 years ago

solution:
Correct answer: Solidification of rocks formed from magmas.

Explanation:

  • When magma cools and solidifies, magnetic minerals in the forming crystals align with the Earth's magnetic field.

  • That alignment is locked into the rock as it solidifies, preserving the direction of the magnetic field at that time.

  • By studying these solidified rocks (for example, ancient lava flows), scientists detected periods when the recorded magnetic direction was opposite to the present field, revealing magnetic reversals.

optionFeedback.html: This is incorrect. The passage does not say that a rapid change from normal to reversed polarity was crucial to the discovery. Instead, the discovery depended on magnetic information preserved in rocks as they formed; the speed of reversal is not presented as the key evidence.

This is partially correct but incomplete. The passage emphasizes that ancient lava flows record the direction of the magnetic field because magnetic minerals in the rock align as the lava cools. The crucial point is the process of rocks forming and trapping magnetic information during solidification, not only that lava flows point to magnetic north.

Correct. As magma cools and solidifies, atoms in the crystals of the rock align with the Earth's magnetic field and lock that orientation into the rock. Studying these solidified rocks (for example, ancient lava flows) allowed scientists to detect times when the magnetic field was reversed.

This is incorrect. The passage mentions that reversals have been correlated with extinctions in the geologic past, but extinctions are described as possible effects or correlations, not as the evidence that led to the discovery of magnetic reversals.

title: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Two paradoxes inform and problematize every discursive and practical employment of "human rights". The first is substantive and directly political: it concerns the relation between "the human" and "the political", and belongs to the domain of political ethics in general. The other is more nearly epistemological and moral; it addresses the issue of how one understands and practices the relationship between idea and actuality, or moral universality and cultural relativity. Each stems from the fact that human rights would cobble together two kinds of concepts and practical relations that are not innately friendly and treats them as one, ignoring the inherent absence of complementarity in their relationship. Thus, the discourse of human rights synthesizes and occludes paradoxical features of the origins, history and character of human rights as an idea and a practice, making it far from self-evident as a conceptual "thing" or guide to moral and political practice. Paradox has always marked the invocation of human rights. Since their discursive inception, the initial paradoxes have not been solved so much as layered by new iterations of them - namely, that initiated in the UDHR (Universal Declaration of Human Rights), which identifies governments as the promissories for enforcement of human rights. Joining the paradoxes is an overarching feature that articulates human rights as a trans-political phenomenon besides being a political phenomenon designed to uplift all human societies.

Ques: What is missing in the discourse of human rights?
solution: The relevant line says that the discourse of human rights synthesizes and occludes paradoxical features, making human rights “far from self-evident” as a conceptual thing or guide to moral and political practice. Therefore what is missing is self-evidence as a concept.

optionFeedback.html: Correct. The passage says the discourse makes human rights “far from self-evident” as a conceptual thing or as a guide to practice.
Incorrect. The passage says paradoxical features are synthesized and occluded; they are not what is missing.
Incorrect. The passage does not say that human-rights features are excluded. It says the discourse is not self-evident as a concept.
Incorrect. Synthesis of concept and practice is part of what the discourse does; the missing element is self-evidence as a concept.

title: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow

In the narrowest sense, price is the amount of money charged for a product or a service. More broadly, price is the sum of all the values that customers give up to gain the benefits of having or using a product or service.

Historically, price has been the major factor affecting buyer choice.

In recent decades, however, nonprice factors have gained increasing importance.

Even so, price remains one of the most important elements that determines a firm's market share and profitability.

Price is the only element in the marketing mix that produces revenue: all other elements present costs. Price is also one of the most flexible marketing mix elements. Unlike product features and channel commitments, prices can be changed quickly.

At the same time, pricing is the number one problem facing many marketing executives, and many companies do not handle pricing well. Some managers view pricing as a big headache, preferring instead to focus on other marketing mix elements.

However, smart managers treat pricing as a key strategic tool for creating and capturing customer value. Prices have a direct impact on a firm's bottom line. A small percentage improvement in price can generate a large percentage increase in profitability. More important, as part of a company's overall value proposition, price plays a key role in creating customer value and building customer relationships.

"Instead of running away from pricing," says an expert, "savvy marketers are embracing it".

The price the company charges will fall somewhere between one that is too low to produce a profit and one that is too high to produce any demand. It summarizes the major considerations in setting price.

Customer perceptions of the product's value set the ceiling for prices. If customers perceive that the product's price is greater than its value, they will not buy the product.

Likewise, product costs set the floor for prices. If the company prices the product below its costs, the company's profits will suffer.

In setting its price between these two extremes, the company must consider competitors' strategies and prices, the overall marketing strategy and mix, and the nature of the market and demand.

Question: What are the other factors influencing or setting the price for products or services?
A. Competitors' strategies
B. Overall marketing mix
C. Type of market
D. Pricing from one extreme to the other
E. Predatory pricing strategies

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: The correct answer is A, B and C only. The passage states that after considering the lower limit set by product costs and the upper limit set by customer value, the company must set price between these two extremes by considering three other factors: competitors' strategies and prices, the overall marketing strategy and mix, and the nature/type of market and demand. These match A, B and C. D only describes the range between the two price extremes, and E is not given in the passage as a factor.

optionFeedback.html: Incorrect. D describes the price range between the lower and upper limits, and E is not stated in the passage as a pricing factor. This option also misses B and C.

Correct. The passage says that between the two price extremes, a company must consider competitors' strategies and prices, the overall marketing strategy and mix, and the nature/type of the market and demand. These correspond to A, B and C.
Incorrect. C is supported by the passage, but D is only a description of the price range and E is not mentioned as a factor. A and B are required.
Incorrect. B and C are supported by the passage, but D is not an influencing factor. The option also omits A, competitors' strategies.

title: Read the following passage and answer the questions based on
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage :

Group thinking, often referred to as groupthink, is a psychological phenomenon wherein the desire for
unanimity within a group overrides the motivation to appraise alternative viewpoints critically. It frequently
leads to flawed decision-making because dissent is either internally suppressed or socially penalized. Social
conformity, its close ally, describes the act of aligning one's beliefs or behaviours with those of a majority,
often subconsciously, in pursuit of acceptance or avoidance of conflict. In tightly knit groups—such as
corporate boards, political committees, or academic panels—individual members may refrain from expressing
contrarian ideas, fearing ostracization or reputational risk. Over time, this collective homogeneity breeds
intellectual stagnation, reducing innovation and enhancing vulnerability to strategic errors. The infamous Bay
of Pigs invasion and the Challenger space shuttle disaster are frequently cited as textbook examples of
decisions marred by groupthink. Psychologically, the roots of group conformity lie in our evolutionary
inclination toward tribal belonging, where deviation was historically associated with survival risk. In modern
society, the same instinct manifests through peer pressure, organizational culture, and digital echo chambers.
Algorithms reinforce conformity by curating information bubbles that validate existing biases while filtering
out divergent thought. However, the remedy to such cognitive myopia lies in institutionalizing dissent.
Constructive disagreement, when encouraged within teams or communities, acts as an intellectual safeguard
against tunnel vision. Promoting a culture where counterarguments are respected rather than reprimanded
can lead to more robust, balanced, and resilient decision-making. In an age dominated by viral trends,
polarized discourse, and performative alignment, the courage to question consensus is both rare and
essential. True progress emerges not from blind allegiance to majority norms, but from critical inquiry and the
audacity to challenge the comfortable.

What is the central idea of groupthink as discussed in the passage?
solution: Groupthink occurs when a group values consensus over critique, so that members avoid challenging weak decisions.

optionFeedback.html: Incorrect. The verified answer is Valuing consensus over critique.
Correct. Groupthink values consensus over critique.
Incorrect. The verified answer is Valuing consensus over critique.
Incorrect. The verified answer is Valuing consensus over critique.

title: DSSSB TGT English 24 Aug 2025 5-7 PM Q77
subject: Verbal Ability (English)
topic: Comprehension / Reading Comprehension / Unseen Passages (Critical Reasoning) (Paragraph Questions)
text:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Just as the oceans opened up a new world for clipper ships and Yankee traders, space holds enormous potential for commerce today. The International Space Station (ISS) took 10 years and more than 30 missions to assemble. It is the result of unprecedented scientific and engineering collaboration among five space agencies representing 15 countries. The space station is approximately the size of a football field: a 460-ton, permanently crewed platform orbiting 250 miles above Earth. It is about four times as large as the Russian space station Mir and five times as large as the U.S. Skylab. The idea of a space station was once science fiction, existing only in the imagination until it became clear in the 1940s that construction of such a structure might be attainable by our nation. As the Space Age began in the 1950s, designs of 'space planes' and stations dominated popular media. The first rudimentary station was created in 1969 by the linking of two Russian Soyuz vehicles in space, followed by other stations and developments in space technology until construction began on the ISS in 1998, aided by the first reusable spacecraft ever developed: the American shuttles. Until recently, U.S. research space onboard the ISS had been reserved for mostly government initiatives, but new opportunities for commercial and academic use of the ISS are now available, facilitated by the ISS National Lab.

According to the passage, which of the following options is NOT a fact?

options.html: The space station is approximately the size of a football field.
The ISS took 10 years and more than 30 missions to assemble.
The ISS is five times the size of the Russian space station Mir.
The first station was created by linking two Russian Soyuz vehicles.

solution:
Concept: In a 'which of the following is NOT a fact' passage question, a fact is a detail the passage states accurately; the check is to compare each option's specific number, comparison, or attributed action word-for-word against the passage's own wording, not against what sounds generally plausible.

Application: The passage gives four checkable details: the station's size compared to a football field; the assembly timeline of 10 years and more than 30 missions; the station's size compared to Mir and to Skylab; and the creation of the first rudimentary station by linking two Russian Soyuz vehicles.

Contrast: - Size vs a football field: the passage's own wording states the station is approximately the size of a football field, which is exactly what this option repeats. - Assembly timeline: the passage's own wording gives 10 years and more than 30 missions, which is exactly what this option repeats. - Size vs Mir and Skylab: the passage's own wording attaches a four-times multiple to Mir and a five-times multiple to Skylab; an option that assigns the five-times multiple to Mir has swapped the two comparisons. - First station's creation: the passage's own wording attributes it to linking two Russian Soyuz vehicles, which is exactly what this option repeats.

Cross-check: Re-reading the exact sentence -- 'about four times as large as ... Mir and five times as large as ... Skylab' -- confirms the two multiples are tied to two different stations, not interchangeable.

Result: Only the statement assigning a five-times multiple to Mir departs from the passage's own wording, which reserves that multiple for Skylab, so that is the statement that is NOT a fact.

optionFeedback.html: This claim uses a comparative estimate ("approximately the size of") to describe scale by analogy to a familiar object.
This claim joins two quantified figures, a duration and a count, to describe a single assembly process.
This claim uses a multiplicative comparison ("five times the size") to relate the station to another named space platform.
This claim uses a passive construction with a by-phrase of means ("created by linking") to describe how an earlier station came into being.

text:
Comprehension:
